AI NOTE — C03 MARKER. Not a translation pair. The wylie field carries the printed running head open steps for those of greater capacity (the acip field holds the same string uppercased; not one Tibetan syllable is present), and the English field carries the chapter heading that opens the next part, VII. Developing the Wish for Enlightenment. Two consecutive lines of a part-divider, ingested as one row. Nothing is aligned; the segment is registered so the coverage gate can prove the course complete. Same class as C03:22, 294, 303 (E-071), 430 and C01:39/43/143.

AI NOTE — Outline heading. GMR's English restates the parent heading ('This brings us to the third and final part of the advices on how to take the essence of this life'), supplies 'Here too there are two divisions' around the single word gnyis, and closes by announcing the next stanza ('and is presented in the single verse of the root text which follows'); none of that has Tibetan under it and it is left unwrapped, as are 'lastly', 'one's', 'divisions' and 'The'. sems bskyed pa is kept as the compound GMR renders 'develop the Wish': bskyed is honestly 'develop', but sems ('mind') is nulled rather than banked as 'Wish', since 'Wish' is GMR's rendering of the whole idiom byang chub tu sems bskyed, not of sems alone (cf. the ruling at C03:429). rim par carries its fused terminative: the -r neither starts a syllable nor is unique inside the word, so it cannot be isolated; 'in the' is left unwrapped. tshul is nulled under the ambiguity rule ('how' occurs three times).
C03/c3p153: AI NOTE — Stanza (7) of the root verse. GMR re-lineates freely; the Tibetan's single supplication verb byin gyis rlobs surfaces twice in English ("Bless me to see" and "Grant me then"). Only "Grant me" is wrapped: it heads the clause the verb actually closes ('byongs par byin gyis rlobs, "Grant me then To practice"), and "Bless me" is GMR distributing the imperative backward over the mthong nas clause. The correlative pair ji bzhin du ... de 'dra bar ("just as ... in like manner") is collapsed into the single word "too", left with kyang; "Has fallen in" has no Tibetan of its own. byang chub sems is spanned whole as GMR's standing "Wish for enlightenment", with its two members. The closing colophon zhes pa'i oo ka gcig gsungs has no English at all.

AI NOTE — Prose frame plus a four-line verse citation; the mid-sentence capitals (Were, To, It, And) are line-initial capitals, not sentence starts.The frame is a standard citation formula, de yang … mdo las, "Now, from the Sutra …"; GMR turns the ablative las into the verb "says", so the particle carries no separable English. dpa' byin calques Sanskrit Vīradatta (dpa' hero, byin given); GMR keeps the Sanskrit name, so the compound is left whole. byang chub sems is bodhichitta, GMR's "the Wish for enlightenment", with the two members crossing in English.gzugs mchis na is literally "if it had form": mchis is the honorific existential, which GMR re-verbs as "take on"; the infinitive marker "To" is supplied and left unwrapped. All three genitives (kyi and the bound 'i of pa'i and nam mkha'i) are unrendered: the English holds three instances of "of" and none can be assigned unambiguously.The last line, de ni de bas lhag par 'gyur, is literally "it would become more than that"; GMR recasts it as "And then spill over farther still". Only lhag (exceed, be in excess) is anchored, to "spill over"; de bas ("than that") has no English exponent, so "farther still", de ni and 'gyur are left unwrapped.

AI NOTE — Prose hinge zhes dang , spyod 'jug las introduces a four-line citation from Shantideva's Bodhisattvacharyavatara; the initial capitals mid-sentence are verse lineation, not apparatus. GMR supplies the frame “The book called … too has lines like the following:” at the FRONT of the English, while the Tibetan closes with zhes sogs dang; that frame is a paraphrase of the whole hinge, not an exponent of sogs, so it is left unwrapped. Inside the verse the crossings are the ordinary ones: dge ba gzhan kun is head-first against “All the other Kinds of virtue”, and 'bras bu 'byin is object-before-verb against “Gives forth its fruits”. “like” and “always” each occur twice; the first occurrences sit in GMR's frame and in the unsupported “they always Die”, so eng_order carries the English cursor past them to the occurrences that render bzhin and rtag par. chu shing is literally a water-tree (plantain); “bamboo tree” is the published reading here and in C16:481 and is spanned as it stands.
C03/c3p154: AI NOTE — Verse citation from Atisha (jo bo chen po, the Great Lord). Line-initial capitals are lineation, not sentence starts. GMR renders the two Tibetan meditation verbs (goms, bsgoms pa) with one English verb, so goms is null. dbang gis ("by the force of") has no exponent: GMR's "And so" is a connective he supplied, not a rendering of the instrumental. bdag nyid kyis is literally "by oneself"; GMR reads it as the subject of the verse in the sense of bdag nyid chen po (mahatma), hence "great beings". min is a bare negative copula; only "cannot" of GMR's supplied frame "It cannot be done" is claimed.

AI NOTE — A short prose hinge (zhes pa dang, closing the previous citation) and then a four-line verse from the Lama's own text; the mid-sentence capitals are lineation. The Tibetan runs theg mchog lam gyi gzhung shing, 'the central beam of the path of the supreme way'; GMR inverts it so the beam is spoken first. says, finally, Our, every, That holds up, Of and the articles are GMR's supply and stay unwrapped: gyi binds lam to the beam and comes out as 'That holds up', while 'Of' renders the particle-less theg mchog/lam link.

AI NOTE — Reconciled reading. zhes sogs is the list-closer that points back at the citations just quoted: GMR's 'these and other', with sogs carrying only 'and other'. The noun 'works' is GMR's supplied head for the elided texts and has no Tibetan under it. gsungs pa ltar ('as was stated') is dissolved into the frame 'We can see from ... that' and is nulled rather than banked as 'works'. In the second sentence the Tibetan runs agent - goal - 'dod - phyin chad, which the English inverts, hence the eng_order crossing. byang chub kyi sems bskyed pa 'di is taken whole as 'this Wish for enlightenment', its members inside it. med thabs med, literally 'no way to be without', is GMR's 'never do without'; the supplied 'we can' and 'is something' stay unwrapped.
C03/c3p155: AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one cing-linked sentence which GMR breaks in two. 'di yod na is literally “if/when this is present”: the conditional-temporal na carries “The minute”, the bare demonstrative 'di is “this” alone (“state of mind” is GMR's gloss), and the stative yod has no exponent — “we reach” is inchoative and is left unwrapped rather than banked against it. gang yang ... med is the emphatic negative frame: “at all” and “no”. zhes bya ba'i ming is “the name called X”; English keeps only “title”, so the quotative is null. sras is “Son”; “(or Daughter)” is GMR's own gloss. theg chen pa'i is the genitive of the agent-noun “greater-way person”, which GMR expands to “of people who live the greater way”, with theg chen holding “the greater way” inside it.

AI NOTE — sems 'di med par ('without this Wish') governs the first stretch; GMR turns it into the hinge 'If though we lack this great Wish'. The concessive ji 'dra yod kyang is split across 'it doesn't matter how many ... we might possess', so kyang is left null. bdag med is spanned whole as 'no nature of their own', with bdag and med as members that cross in the English. lta ci ('let alone') and 'tshang rgya ('reach enlightenment') are moved by GMR to the end of the second sentence, which is why the English order crosses so hard here. pas na is causal ('since we won't join...'); GMR's 'And so' opens a new sentence as a supplied consequent hinge and is left unwrapped. sems carries 'Wish' both times; byang chub and bskyed pa have no separate exponent.

AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one temporal clause: de la ... bsgoms pas nges 'byung skyes yod tshe, "at the time when, having meditated on X, renunciation has arisen." Geshe Michael breaks it into two English sentences and supplies the hinge "In this way" at the seam; the causal pas and the final tshe are left without an exponent rather than credited with his connective. skyes bu chung 'bring skabs is literally "the sections of the lesser and medium practitioner"; "the steps that are shared with" and "capacity" are supplied context and stay unwrapped. rang steng du, "upon oneself," is spread across "but relative only to ourselves": only rang has a word to point at. nges 'byung (renunciation) is expanded into "the virtue of a healthy disgust for the kind of life we live"; only "disgust" is claimed.
C03/c3p156: AI NOTE — One long Tibetan period; GMR breaks it into three English sentences and reorders heavily. gzhan steng du kha spos te bsams na is literally 'if, shifting the face (of the meditation) onto others, one contemplates' — GMR expands this into 'take the same thoughts and transfer them--you try to feel them relative to the condition that others are in'. Only others, transfer and feel are pinned; steng du is left null because 'relative to the condition that ... are in' is a supplied paraphrase, not a rendering of 'upon'. sogs ('and so on') is claimed only as 'the other'; 'attitudes' is GMR's gloss and stays unwrapped. ltar ('in accordance with') is 'as'; 'following these methods' is GMR's resumptive with no Tibetan under it. dang is a plain coordinator; GMR's 'or else' is a supplied disjunction and is not banked. The genitive chain byang chub lam rim las gsungs pa ltar gyi man ngag = 'the instruction, as taught in the Steps of the Path to Buddhahood' — GMR moves the whole citation clause to the end of the English, which is why the English order crosses back. gzhan occurs twice and 'others' twice; the second is a member of the compound bdag gzhan.

AI NOTE — Tibetan puts the condition first (once the experience of the Wish has just begun to arise); GMR's English puts the main clause first, so the two sides cross wholesale. The sentence is built on two sogs ("and so on"): the first closes the list of threshold experiences and is rendered "such as"; the second closes the list of things one trains in, and GMR expands it into "all the relevant details" and adds the hinge "an example would be" - neither has Tibetan under it, so both are left unwrapped. smon 'jug gi sems abbreviates smon pa'i sems bskyed and 'jug pa'i sems bskyed; the single sems is distributed over both English occurrences of "the Wish" and is not separately claimed. TCS15:51 has the same idiom sne zin tsam ... skyes pa, rendered there "have reached a good understanding", which is why skyes pa takes "reached".

AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one long dependent chain that GMR breaks into four English sentences. He renders rgya mtsho twice ("the sea of the pain of this suffering life" and "the ocean of the circle of births") and lhung twice ("slipped and fallen", "dropped"); only the unique half of each doublet is spanned ("ocean", "fallen") and the paraphrase half is left unwrapped.na (sickness) in the standard four skye rga na 'chi has no exponent in "birth and getting old and death" and is nulled. drag tu (violently) is nulled: GMR's "great" modifies the sea-waves, not the raging. mi mngon ("is not apparent") is rendered "I cannot even guess"; mi takes "cannot", mngon "guess", and the supplied "even" stays bare.
C03/c3p157: AI NOTE — The Tibetan opens with the enumeration of the three sufferings and only then names the sea monsters; GMR inverts this, putting the creatures first and the list in apposition after the semicolon, hence the heavy crossing. du mas ('many', agentive) surfaces as GMR's idiom 'A great host of' and is left unbanked: the article and the noun have no Tibetan under them. sdug bsngal bzod dka' bas (the suffering hard to bear) has no separate exponent, and the closing simile frame ji lta ba de bzhin du is dropped by GMR. 'rise up and', 'They rip at me', 'relentlessly' and the supplied pronouns 'me'/'they' are translator's amplification and stay unwrapped.

AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one nominal chain whose head is 'gro ba kun te ("all beings") at the very end; everything before it is relative material: those who, from beginningless lifetimes, by way of great kindness, again and again nurtured (me) and became (my) mother. GMR unrolls the chain into two English sentences and reverses its order, so the head noun surfaces first. The connective prose ("And the same thing is happening to", "Every one of them has in the past", "string of", "I have lived through", "they cared for me and", "my own") has no Tibetan under it and is left unwrapped. yang dang yang du ("again and again") has no English exponent at all; sgo nas ("by way of") survives only as the preposition "with".

AI NOTE — GMR expands one Tibetan sentence into five English ones, so the crossings are heavy. Everything up to dgod is the content of a thought closed by snyam du; GMR's three I must frames render that thinking, not any one word, so snyam is left null rather than banked as resolve. dgod is causative ('to place them in'); GMR's will see to it that every one of them climbs turns the beings into the subject, and climbs alone would teach a false meaning, so it is null. Also unwrapped: de dang 'dra bar ('just like that') inside have fallen in too, where only kyang = too is claimable; bcas pa and the ablative las, whose exponents and / from are too common to pin. rag las 'depend' is one verb split by the negation, so depending sits on las with rag nulled.
C03/c3p158: AI NOTE — One enormous nominalised request: everything up to gsol ba btab pa modifies blo, and GMR breaks it into three English sentences each headed by "we are asking". So the main verb gsol ba btab pa has three exponents and none can be claimed, and blo is dissolved into "states of mind" / "the ability" with no assignable exponent; both are nulled. gyis is banked as "by" because "plagued by suffering" renders the instrumental directly. 'byongs pa (become proficient) is banked as "practice": GMR's three verbs after "the ability to" answer to goms pa, 'byongs pa and yongs su rdzogs pa. bcos ma ma yin par uses the negative-affix convention: ma yin par owns the "un" of "uncontrived" and bcos ma the stem. byang chub sems is taken whole as "Wish for enlightenment" because bare "Wish" occurs twice; its two members resolve inside it. ga rang is the emphatic in "this very seat".

AI NOTE — An outline heading. GMR's first sentence restates the PARENT headings ("the instruction on how to train one's mind in the Steps of the path for persons of greater spiritual capacity") and has no Tibetan under it here beyond gnyis pa; his closing clause ("and is presented in a single verse of the root text") is apparatus introducing the next stanza. Both are left unwrapped. The Tibetan restates its own heading in full at mdo phyogs kyi spyod pa la slob pa'i tshul, which GMR compresses to "The former"; those words are marked null rather than attached to English that belongs to the earlier occurrence. tshul ("the way of") appears five times and is rendered only once, as the "how" of "explains how to train oneself" in the last clause; the "how" of the first sentence belongs to the restated parent heading, not to this row.

AI NOTE — The stanza is one Tibetan sentence hung on a single verb of request, byin gyis rlobs. GMR splits it into two English imperatives — “Bless me to see clearly…” and “Grant me then…” — so the one verb has two candidate exponents and only one may be banked. The complement that actually hangs off byin gyis rlobs is brtson pa drag pos slob par, “to train with fierce effort,” which surfaces under “Grant me then A fierce resolve To master the vows”; so the verb is aligned to “Grant me” and “Bless me” stays unwrapped as GMR's supplied second imperative.sems…bskyed is the standard compound for generating the Wish for enlightenment, but tsam (“merely, itself”) is wedged between its members, so it cannot be spanned whole; the head sems carries “Wish” and the verb bskyed is nulled. The concessive kyang is what GMR turns into the whole predicate “Is not enough”; that is a recasting, not a lexical exponent, so it is nulled and the phrase left unwrapped. med is nulled because “not” occurs twice in the English with no way to resolve which is which. mi is aligned to “cannot”: the Tibetan carries only the negation, and the modality of “can” is GMR's reading of the future negative mi 'grub, “will not be accomplished” — but “cannot” is a single indivisible word that exists only to render that negation.rgyal sras, literally “son(s) of the Victor,” is a compound whose two members both surface in GMR's “children of the Victors,” in reverse order. legs par here is adverbial “well,” rendered “clearly”; the “well” in “well trained” is GMR's supplement and is not claimed. The trailing zhes pa'i oo ka gcig ste, “that is one verse,” is editorial apparatus with no English.
C03/c3p159: AI NOTE — One long Tibetan conditional — even though you generate a mere mind hoping for buddhahood for the sake of beings, without training in the six perfections you will not awaken — which GMR breaks into five English sentences, so several hinges have no single word under them: kyang becomes “This itself is not enough,” and the negation ma … mi becomes “Otherwise there is no way.” “The Wish (for enlightenment)” is GMR's term for bodhicitta; the wylie has no byang chub, so bare sems (mind) is not given “Wish” — only the idiom sems bskyed, taken whole, is matched to “reach the Wish.” drug (six) is left unwrapped because GMR counts the other five beside giving. The wylie reads spyin where the independent witness C07:80 reads sbyin (giving); see errata.

AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one consequential sentence, des na ... ste. des na means only 'therefore'; GMR recasts it as a full clause, This fact explains why, whose subject and verb are his own supply, so the hinge is left unwrapped rather than banked on the particle. He also fronts the evaluation (ha cang gnad che, 'so very important') that the Tibetan holds to the end.gsungs is the honorific of 'say'; that honorific is what licenses GMR's holy beings, but no agent noun stands in the wylie, so only said is wrapped. 'dir ('here', in this context) is unrendered. phar phyin drug and rnam pa gsum both put the numeral after the noun and the English reverses both. all, the, of, it is, when, that, are, have are GMR's supplied English.

AI NOTE — The wylie is a fragment of a running definition (C07:82 carries the same passage, continuing with thog), and GMR's English re-orders it almost completely. Tibetan order: spyir ser skya gang yin yang nges par bsrung dgos pa'i ('in general, whether robed or lay, must definitely be kept'), bsrung bya thun mong ba ('the common object of keeping'), mi dge bcu spong gi tshul khrims legs par bsrung ba'i ('of keeping well the morality of abandoning the ten non-virtues'). GMR states the object first and the scope last. ser skya is literally 'saffron and white', the ordained and the lay; GMR renders the pair idiomatically as 'whether they wear the robes or not', of which only 'robes' is claimed here, with gang yin yang supplying 'whether' and 'wear ... or not' left as GMR's periphrasis. legs par ('well') is taken as 'careful'; 'extremely' is GMR's intensifier with no Tibetan under it. The opening sentence, 'The first type is called the "morality of keeping oneself from committing wrong,"' has no Tibetan under it in this row and is left unwrapped.
C03/c3p16: AI NOTE — Relay #8 closes. slob / mi slob → "those on the paths of learning / done learning" (the technical śaik⋅a pair); rang rgyal → "Self-Made" (28 consistency); sras → "Sons and Daughters" (35 consistency). The delayed English transforms s45rest's simile: dbul pos gter rnyed pa ltar ("like a pauper finding treasure") → "like a beggar who has stumbled across a mine of gold" (gter → a gold mine). ENGLISH QUEUE C03-#5: a STRAY DUPLICATE "[d]" appears mid-segment after the verse bracket — the list-marker reprinted; artifact, kept verbatim.

AI NOTE — ca/ ↔ "[e]" — letter-numeral #5. The ingredient title itself is a FOUR-UNIT MIRROR (w4-w3-w2-w1: yan lag / bskul / bskor / chos 'khor → ingredient / urging / to turn / the Wheel). Citation mirror with crosswise quote again ('"Who' ← gang rnams before "in all the ten directions" ← phyogs bcu'i). s47rest: the recently-enlightened with unstoppable knowledge, and Yeshe De's variant reading — English in 48.

AI NOTE — THE TRANSLATOR'S FIRST-PERSON VOICE: the closing bracket — '[rather than "taken each of the steps to Buddhahood," and I have followed him.]' — is GMR adjudicating between root-text readings on Yeshe De's authority, in his own voice. sgron ma → "Lamps"; 'jig rten → "the worlds" (3rd render: planets / circle of life / worlds); mgon po → "Saviors"; ma chags → "The state beyond desire"; bskul crosses L4→L3 ("I urge"); w9-w8-w7 three-unit mirror inside L2. WYLIE QUEUE: "dag,byang" missing comma-space.
C03/c3p160: AI NOTE — The wylie opens with a fused token, thogbye brag tu. The parallel witness C07:83 reads bye brag tu ("more specifically"), and its preceding segment C07:82 ends ...legs par bsrung ba'i thog, where C03:498 ends ...legs par bsrung ba'i with no thog. The syllable thog therefore belongs to the previous sentence and has migrated across the segment break. The first span quotes the corruption verbatim, so it carries one stray syllable; only bye brag tu is rendered by "More specifically". See errata.The English is heavily reordered against the Tibetan. Tibetan front-loads the three vow-sets (so thar, byang sems, gsang sngags) and only then names them collectively as sdom pa gsum; GMR moves the whole list to a trailing sentence. The category name nyes spyod sdom pa'i tshul khrims (the morality of restraining from bad conduct) closes the Tibetan but is front-loaded by GMR as "this first type of morality", so only tshul khrims is aligned.

AI NOTE — The wylie is a single defining noun phrase whose head, dge ba'i chos sdud pa'i tshul khrims, stands last; GMR fronts it as the quoted name ("morality of collecting goodness") and then unpacks the long modifier before it, so the English crosses almost completely. The head is aligned as one compound so that tshul khrims can be matched to the "morality" inside the quoted name rather than to the first "morality", which belongs to GMR's supplied frame "The second type of morality is known as the" and has no Tibetan under it. tshogs gnyis ("the two collections"), chos, and sgo nas ("by way of") are left null: the English keeps the members of the pair but not the collective noun, and "use" is GMR's own finite verb rather than a rendering of the postposition.

AI NOTE — GMR front-loads the Tibetan predicate: the whole first English sentence renders the tail sems can don byed kyi tshul khrims yin pas, so the English order runs nearly backwards against the wylie. "The third type of", "every", "Here you take care to", "yourself from wrong" and "which is" are supplied framing with no Tibetan under them and are left unwrapped. ma is nulled because GMR turns the negated ma bslad ("unadulterated by") into the positive relative clause "which is infected" under the supplied hinge "instead of", so the negation has no exponent to own. ched du is a purpose marker ("for the sake of"); GMR renders it as the motive preposition "out of", which is the only exponent of that relation in the English.
C03/c3p161: AI NOTE — One long Tibetan conditional nominalisation ending in rnyed nas; GMR fronts the main clause ("You must find a sure kind of knowledge") and hangs the whole de lta bu'i ... mi 'grub par condition off "where you see clearly how", so nearly every content word crosses. nges pa brtan po ("firm certainty") is rendered "a sure kind of knowledge": the head noun nges pa takes "knowledge" and the adjective brtan po (firm, steady, sure) takes "sure"; GMR's hinge "kind of" is left unwrapped. The formula bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub ("unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment") is compressed to "the fully enlightened state of a Buddha": "fully" goes to rdzogs pa (complete), while bla na med pa and yang dag par have no exponent and are nulled. myong ba chen po, literally "a great experience", is rendered idiomatically as "a total fluency". The conditional na is nulled because GMR writes "if" twice for one Tibetan marker.

AI NOTE — The Tibetan fronts the object, rgyal ba'i sras te byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa, and defers the verb bzung; the English inverts this, so the alignment crosses. Once you have found this knowledge and the hinge and then have no Tibetan under them. GMR renders the vow-name twice, once as a gloss (the vows for the "children of the Victors") and once literally (the bodhisattva vows); only the literal rendering is wrapped as the compound. brtson pa is in the dictionary effort or diligence; resolve is GMR's rendering of it in this sentence, banked as his choice, not as a gloss. slob is expanded to learn and master, and only learn is claimed. our Lama after said is supplied by the translator; the honorific gsungs is claimed only for said. The frame What we are requesting of our Lama here ... is that he or she is a periphrasis of the honorific imperative; only grant is claimed for byin gyis rlobs.

AI NOTE — A one-line outline heading. GMR's English is far longer than the Tibetan because he restates the position in the outline (Having presented the bodhisattva activities in general, we will now turn to...) and adds his own apparatus sentence about the single root-text verse that follows. Only the heading proper — the final two perfections and the manner of training in them — has Tibetan under it. gnyis pa is the outline number 'second', which GMR does not translate; slob tshul is 'the way of training', rendered 'how to train', with 'oneself' as GMR's supplied object.
C03/c3p162: AI NOTE — Stanza (9) of the root verse; the '(9)' is GMR's apparatus and the initial capitals mid-sentence are verse lineation. GMR inverts the stanza wholesale: the Tibetan opens with the two qualifying lines (zhi byed / dpyod pa) and closes with the petition (byin gyis rlobs), while the English opens with the petition and appends the two qualities as 'One which ... The other which'. Per campaign precedent byin gyis rlobs takes a single exponent, 'Grant that'; the complement 'I may' is GMR's supplied hinge and stays unwrapped, as do the articles 'The' and the preposition 'In the'. rgyud la skye bar ('arise in the mind-stream') is compressed by GMR to 'gain', which is banked on the verb skye bar alone; rgyud has no exponent. The closing prose frame zhes pa'i oo ka gcig gis bstan ('this is taught by one shloka') is untranslated in this row.

AI NOTE — GMR reads log pa'i yul as the verse's phrase and glosses it with phyin ci log gi yul, 'mistaken objects'; the gloss idiom zhes pa ... la bya dgos ('the term X must be applied to Y') becomes 'should be understood as referring to', so only the modal dgos is banked. The example is the non-Buddhist (phyi rol pa) fixing the mind on pebbles, wood and the like (rdel shing sogs), which GMR collapses to a single 'short stick of wood'. de 'dra'i modifies sems ('such a mind'); GMR moves the demonstrative onto the objects as 'these types of', so it is left unmapped. The verb pair zhi ba'am med par byed ('makes quiet, or makes non-existent') produces his doubled '"quiet" the mind--that is, stop the mind'; the second sems takes the first of those two 'mind's, the repetition is left unwrapped.

AI NOTE — One Tibetan sentence ending lta bu min par: everything up to bshad pa is the position being rejected, and lta bu min par rejects it. GMR breaks it into three English sentences and renders the rejection structurally, with the hinge "--except", which is left unwrapped: no Tibetan word means "except". The analytic clause sems zhes pa ... ma rnyed pa'i, Tibetan-initial, is pushed to the very end of the English, so the second half crosses heavily. GMR's expansions ("of the past too", "schools", "moving in this stupor to a realization of", "they describe this emptiness as what you come to", the second "then") have no Tibetan exponent and stay unwrapped.
C03/c3p163: AI NOTE — The Tibetan runs owner-first: rgyal tshab byams pa'i (the Regent, the Loving One = Maitreya) owns dbus mtha' rnam 'byed (the Madhyanta-vibhanga), whose man ngag are said (gsungs pa) in rje'i lam rim che chung sogs - Je Tsongkapa's greater and lesser Steps and the like. GMR unwinds this head-last chain head-first and prefixes a rebuttal of his own (But none of these ideas is correct; rather, we must follow texts), which has no Tibetan under it and is left unwrapped; ltar ('in accordance with') is therefore unrendered - there is no 'as' here, and 'follow' is the verb of the supplied clause, as at C03:487. che chung is 'big-small' but GMR gives 'briefer and more expanded', so the members cross inside their own parent. The bound genitives on byams pa'i and rje'i are left out; 'the Great' and 'himself' are honorific additions.

AI NOTE — One long serial construction: three coordinated actions (spong / bsten pa / bsgrubs) with the qualifier yid byed bzhi dang ldan pa'i standing attributively before sems gnas pa dgu. GMR moves that qualifier to the tail ("complete with their four different modes") and lifts rim bzhin ("in steps") to the head of the clause, so the English crosses the Tibetan at both ends. gnyen po 'du byed brgyad is split across "eight corrective actions" by position: gnyen po = "corrective", 'du byed = "actions" (GMR's contextual rendering of samskara). yid byed (manaskara, mental engagement) is rendered loosely as "modes"; "different" is GMR's own. The comitative dang owns "with" and ldan pa owns "complete". The frame "These treatises describe how one progresses", "to meditation", "their", "different" and the articles have no Tibetan under them and stay unwrapped; the genitive 'i does not start a syllable and is not spanned.

AI NOTE — GMR recasts one Tibetan nominal clause as two English sentences. The Tibetan runs modifier-first (virtuous object → one-pointed placement → pliancy-bliss → quietude); the English leads with the result (bliss) and trails the cause. des drangs pa'i zhi gnas (“the quietude drawn forth by that”) becomes the independent sentence This then leads to … quietude: the relative framing is dissolved but the causal direction (bliss → quietude) is preserved, so des = This and drangs = leads to. GMR's One thus attains a kind of, which comes from, meditation on, one chooses and what we call are supplied hinges with no separable Tibetan under them and are left unwrapped.
C03/c3p164: AI NOTE — One long definition of lhag mthong, perfect insight: a chain of qualifiers ending in the head noun, which GMR unwinds into four English sentences, so the English crosses the Tibetan repeatedly. yang dag ste cites a lemma from the root verse; GMR's gloss "perfect meaning" supplies "meaning" from the verse's own don, which is not in this wylie, so only "perfect" is claimed. No English exponent for lus (body), shin sbyangs (pliancy), brten nas (absorbed into 'This brings on') or bsgom pa.

AI NOTE — One long Tibetan sentence built on la brten nas — ‘relying upon’ a practice in which quietude and insight are never parted — which GMR splits into two English sentences, moving the request verb (gsol ba btab pa) from the very end of the Tibetan to the front of his second sentence. The pair is named twice: zhi gnas dang lhag mthong in full, then abbreviated to zhi lhag, which GMR expands to ‘meditative quietude and perfect insight’ — only the head nouns have Tibetan under them. skye ba is intransitive (‘arise’ in the mindstream); GMR’s transitive ‘gain’ is the same event with us as agent. ‘We seek to’, ‘process’, ‘our Lama’, ‘the verse’, ‘as a result’ and ‘form of’ are supplied by the translator and carry no Tibetan.

AI NOTE — C03 MARKER. Not a translation pair. The wylie field carries the printed running head secret steps for those of greater capacity (the acip field holds the same string uppercased; not one Tibetan syllable is present), and the English field carries the chapter heading that opens the next part, X. Entering the Way of the Diamond. Two consecutive lines of a part-divider, ingested as one row. Nothing is aligned; the segment is registered so the coverage gate can prove the course complete. C03/c3p165: AI NOTE — An outline heading. The Tibetan is a bare three-way division - sngags phyogs kyi spyod pa la slob pa'i tshul la gsum, "the way of training in the practices of the secret side: three" - followed by the three items and the tag dang po ni. GMR expands it into running prose. His opening hinge ("This brings us to ... our discussion about the activities of a bodhisattva") restates the parent heading and has no Tibetan under it; spyod pa is claimed at its in-phrase exponent "endeavors", not at the restated "activities". tshul occurs three times: the first is the head noun that gsum counts, and GMR's capitalised "Steps" is the head noun that "three" counts, so it is banked as his outline rendering of 'ways'; the other two are rendered by "how to", which occurs three times and cannot be pinned, so they are nulled. gsum itself is nulled: "three" occurs twice in the English. The closing sentence ("The first of these three is presented in the single verse of the root text which follows") is GMR's apparatus for dang po ni; only "The first" is claimed inside it.

AI NOTE — Stanza (10) of the root text, a four-line supplication: the conditional thun mong lam sbyangs snod du gyur pa na, the object of entry (theg pa kun gyi mchog gyur rdo rje'i theg / skal bzang skye bo'i 'jug ngogs dam pa der), then manner and verb bde blag nyid du 'jug par, closed by byin gyis rlobs. GMR fronts the verb as "Grant that" and re-lineates, so the English crosses the Tibetan heavily; byin gyis rlobs takes the single exponent "Grant" and its complement 'jug par surfaces as "I enter". 'jug ngogs is kept whole with both members inside it since GMR's "door to come inside" reverses the compound. "For the fortunate and the good" is GMR's doublet on skal bzang (cf. C03:522, "people who are so fortunate and good"); only "fortunate" is banked and skye bo is nulled. "that is worthy", "well", "perfect" and the supplied "I", "The", "of", "with", "For" have no Tibetan under them and stay unwrapped. The closing frame zhes pa'i oo ka gcig gsungs te has no English in this row.

AI NOTE — GMR expands one Tibetan sentence into four English ones, so the English crosses hard. med du mi rung ba'i (indispensable) is given only "you could never succeed without them"; GMR's hinge "so important for both that" is left unwrapped. lam is spanned twice: "the path" of the shared Steps and the member "paths" inside lam gyi gtso bo rnam gsum. legs par is nulled only because "well" occurs twice against one Tibetan source. sngon du song nas (having gone before) is not "On top of this", and gyur pa (become) is not "make": both are nulled rather than banked against GMR's restructured connectives. de'i tshe na (in that case) is given only "then"; "These" is GMR's supplied subject.
C03/c3p166: AI NOTE — The wylie runs qualifier-first: the distinguishing feature ('bras bu lam du byed pa sogs yod pa'i cha nas, "from the standpoint of having such features as taking the goal as the path") opens the sentence, then the list of lesser vehicles, then the superlative, and only at the end the vehicle entered and the modal 'jug dgos. GMR inverts this wholesale, leading with the injunction and closing with the feature, so nearly every span crosses. He renders gsang sngags rdo rje'i theg pa as two English mentions ("Way of the Diamond", then "which is to say, this Way of the Secret Word") and re-mentions it a third time as "the Diamond Way" inside a framing clause of his own; the spans claim the first mention for rdo rje'i theg pa and "the Secret Word" for gsang sngags, leaving the hinge and the resumptive third mention unwrapped. yod pa'i cha nas is left unclaimed: no contiguous English string is honestly its rendering.

AI NOTE — A gloss on one word. rdo rje'i skad dod badzr = 'the equivalent term for rdo rje is badzr'; GMR splits it over two English sentences, so skad dod lands on the 'word' of 'the Sanskrit word vajra' (the equivalent-word), and 'Sanskrit', 'translation' and 'This is a' are GMR's framing. badzr is the Tibetan transcription of Sanskrit vajra, not a misspelling. The etymology is dbyer mi phyed pa la 'jug pa, 'applies to what cannot be divided' — 'has the basic meaning of "inseparable"'. Two referents follow: (1) the ting nge 'dzin that is like the thugs rdo rje, the diamond of the Buddha's holy mind; (2) the ye shes in which thabs (great bliss) and shes rab (emptiness) are gnyis dbyer mi phyed pa, 'the two undivided'. GMR's 'combination' renders that whole phrase, so gnyis ('two') is left unwrapped rather than banked as 'combination'; likewise 'which is' is a relative-clause copula GMR supplied, not yin, and 'also' is not nam ('or').

AI NOTE — A gloss on theg pa: it is the ming (name, word) of bzhon pa, a conveyance one rides. ming is matched to "word" (its dictionary sense); the two quotative zhes pa around it and "has a meaning of" are GMR's restructuring and stay unwrapped. pa'ang ("as well") is bound to the syllable and has no wrappable shape; pas and phyir are causal in the Tibetan while GMR's "thus" and "in order to" run different inferences, so both are nulled rather than banked. yun (duration) is not "eons": the eons are the ellipsed bskal pa of grangs med. "--something you get on and ride to reach a destination" and the hinges "here", "the", "his", "any sort of" are GMR-supplied and left unwrapped.
C03/c3p167: AI NOTE — AI NOTE: gsang sngags rdo rje'i theg pa is one title; GMR reverses its halves into “the Diamond Way, the Way of the Secret Word,” so the English crosses at the start. tshe thung gcig is rendered twice (“but one lifetime” / “one of the very short kinds of life”); it is banked once, against the first rendering: tshe = “lifetime”, with thung and gcig left unmapped. tsam, the restrictive hedge, is what licenses “no more than”; the “in” that carries gyi ring la is GMR's own hinge. rta ... bang rtsal can collapses into the single word “racehorse”, which cannot be split, so only bzang po = “fine” is claimed there.

AI NOTE — One Tibetan sentence, a dang-joined contrast between two parties each marked rnams kyis and each closing on skal ba: skal ba dman pa (a deficient lot) against skal ba bzang po dang ldan pa (endowed with a fine one). GMR renders it as four English sentences. The genitive phrase rang nyid gcig pu'i qualifies zhi bde in the Tibetan ("the peace of themselves alone"); GMR floats it into its own clause, "and this too only for themselves", so rang nyid and gcig pu'i are aligned as words and the 'for' is left as GMR's. don gnyis mthar phyin pa'i sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang is expanded into a coordinate pair, "the state of a perfect Buddha, and the ability to fulfil, totally, the ultimate needs of both others and themselves": mthar phyin takes "fulfil" ("perfect" and "totally" are GMR's doublings of it), don gnyis takes "needs of both" ("others and themselves" spells out the two). sgrub pa'i is nulled: "enables them to reach" is a causative recast with no Tibetan word under "enables them". Supplied with no Tibetan under them and left unwrapped: "The kinds of practitioners that we call", the first "only to reach a state of", "therefore", "kind of good virtue that makes one want", "on the other hand", "wonderful", "the ability to", "ultimate".

AI NOTE — The Tibetan is one long supplication read as a gloss: de lta'i skal bzang skye bo byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi 'jug ngogs — "the entry-ford of the bodhisattvas, such fortunate beings" — which is then qualified as sgo dam pa'am mchog tu gyur pa, "the holy or supreme door." GMR leads with the qualifier ("the 'holiest' (meaning highest) door, or gateway") and puts the beneficiaries after it, so "door, or gateway" answers two separate Tibetan nouns and nearly the whole first sentence crosses.gsang sngags rdo rje theg pa is one title — the Diamond Way of the Secret Word — and GMR splits it into two apposed phrases both times it appears, rendering rdo rje theg pa'i as "the Diamond Way" first and "the Way of the Diamond" second; lam is "path" in both places.nos pas ("having received") is rendered twice over by GMR ("receiving the four empowerments ... and receiving them perfectly"); the alignment points at the second, which sits beside legs par "perfectly"; "them" is GMR's pronoun for the empowerments and is left unwrapped. de lta bur ("such a") is left unaligned: "just described" is GMR's contextual expansion, not an equation. Supplied hinges ("What is", "It is", "so that they are", "What we are requesting in this verse then", "our Lama", "with") have no Tibetan under them.
C03/c3p168: AI NOTE — Flat walk. GMR's frame ("With this we have reached the ... Step to training oneself in the secret half of the bodhisattva activities; that is,") and the closing sentence about the root-text verse have no Tibetan under them and stay unwrapped. dbang dus kyi is expanded to the relative clause "when he received his secret empowerment"; only "when" (dus, time) and "empowerment" (dbang) are claimed. dag par bya ba'i = "to make pure": "pure" is dag; "keep" is GMR's rendering of the verb construction and is left unwrapped rather than banked as a gloss of bya ba.

AI NOTE — Verse citation (four lines marked by the , , shad pairs) with a prose tail. GMR's English radically re-orders the Tibetan: the line-4 petition byin gyis rlobs is fronted as 'Bless', and line 3 ('genuine certainty') precedes lines 1-2. The prose tail zhes pa'i oo ka gcig gis bstan cing is left unwrapped: it has no exponent in this row's English. (11) is a caption number; the verse-line initial capitals (With, That, The, Both, Is, And, Grant, To, Even) are lineation. Left unwrapped as GMR's supplied tissue: 'me' (twice), 'know', 'I've entered thus', 'gives', 'the', 'my', 'Is keeping', 'Grant me then', 'always', 'them', 'Even if'. rnam da is quoted byte-for-byte; the independent witnesses TCS13:729 and TCS08:12 read rnam dag - see errata.

AI NOTE — The wylie ends at de'i tshe; the English runs on into a second sentence ("If you then follow the correct method...") whose Tibetan sits in the following segment, and it is left unwrapped. de yang and gyur are nulled: "Now suppose you have entered thus" and "have made yourself" are GMR's recap hinge and causative recast, not exponents. rdo rje theg pa is wrapped whole because "Way" occurs twice; the second ("the Way of the Secret Word") is GMR's expansion, not a second theg pa. "different" and "which is" are supplied and stay unwrapped.
C03/c3p169: AI NOTE — GMR splits one Tibetan noun phrase into two English sentences: mchog gi dngos grub = 'The ultimate attainment', and the appositional rgyal ba rdo rje 'chang gi go 'phang = 'the state of the Victorious One, the Keeper of the Diamond' (Vajradhara). The hinges is reaching, where there is, This is and the qualifier secret are GMR's supplied English with no Tibetan under them and stay unwrapped. mi slob pa (Skt. aśaikṣa, the no-more-learning stage) is taken whole as 'nothing more to be learned'; the negation is not split off, since nothing is not one of the four sanctioned negative affixes. dang shows the segment continues a list into the next line.

AI NOTE — A list row. The wylie names the eight items first and closes with the topic phrase thun mongs gi dngos grub; GMR front-loads the topic (The shared attainments are those such as the "eight great attainments.") and ends with the list, so the English side crosses completely. dngos grub occurs twice: the first (after mkha' spyod kyi) is rendered "special powers"; the second is the member of thun mongs gi dngos grub rendered "attainments". bcas closes the list and is left null: "These include", "known as", "are those" and the articles are GMR's supplied hinges with no Tibetan exponent. The genitive 'i on pa'i is bound and left unwrapped.

AI NOTE — GMR renders the opening rhetorical question freely: dngos grub rnam pa gnyis gang las sgrub pa'i gzhi'am ('the basis from which the two kinds of attainment are accomplished, or...') becomes 'What then is it that can give you these attainments? Their cause or foundation'. Only gang ('What') and gzhi ('foundation') are separably attachable; 'cause' and 'can give you' paraphrase the relative clause gang las sgrub pa'i as a whole and are left unwrapped, as is the disjunctive 'am ('or'), bound to gzhi in the wylie. rnam pa gnyis ('the two kinds', common and supreme attainments) has no exponent. The second gang is the relative 'which'. The three dang and yin pas are unresolvable against repeated 'and'/'is'.
C03/c3p17: AI NOTE — cha/ ↔ "[f]" — letter-numeral #6. mya ngan 'da' ston → "pretend to pass into nirvana" — ston ("show, display") rendered "pretend": the docetic display of dying made blunt English. Citation mirror as usual. s49rest (staying for atom-count eons, bodies beyond counting) waits for 50.

AI NOTE — Rotation 4-1-2-3 (the liturgical standard), with a THREE-UNIT MIRROR opening (w3-w2-w1: To all of those / who may intend / To pretend…). TWO "Stay"s in English, ONE bzhugs in Tibetan: the first ("Stay, I pray") is supplied anticipation, unwrapped; the wrapped "Stay" is bzhugs par yang. "at my breast" SUPPLIED (thal mo rab sbyar has no breast); press/palms crossed (w14 before w13). The tail runs w10-w9-w8 mirrored ("equal in number To the atoms of every world").

AI NOTE — ja/ ↔ "[g]" — THE LETTER-NUMERAL SEQUENCE COMPLETES: ka kha ga nga ca cha ja = [a]–[g], one per ingredient. The citation quote even keeps the trailing particle: phyag 'tshal ba dang → '"prostrations and..."'. The long s51rest is the SUMMARY TAXONOMY of all seven ingredients (five = gathering the conducive; confession = purifying the obstacles; rejoicing partly increases one's own virtue; dedication makes the small vast and the exhaustible inexhaustible — bsag / sbyang / spel / mi zad) — its English arrives in the following segments.
C03/c3p170: AI NOTE — GMR unfolds one Tibetan sentence into three English ones: the clause-final tshul bzhin bsrung dgos becomes the opening summary ("We must ... honor and keep, just as we are required"), then the vow-sets are unpacked in Tibetan order. tshul bzhin and bsrung each surface twice (also 'perfectly', 'being sure to honor'); one rendering each is banked. dam tshig is anchored to the third-sentence 'pledges', whose neighbors ('general', 'individual', 'Five Classes') are its Tibetan neighbors; 'vows' in 'vows and pledges' is GMR-supplied (no sdom pa) and is not claimed. gzhan yang and rnams have no separable exponent.

AI NOTE — GMR inverts the Tibetan wholesale: the wylie lists the four doors first and ends with the negated main verb (bsrung mi nus); the English opens with the main clause and appends the list as a second sentence. 'all your pledges and vows' (object of bsrung), the hinge 'unless you manage to' and 'through which' are supplied by GMR with no Tibetan under them and are left unwrapped. mang ba (many, abundant) is nulled: GMR's 'particularly severe' is a contextual rendering, not this word's equivalent.

AI NOTE — One Tibetan sentence — a tshul ni ... rnams yin cing list of four ways — recast by GMR as four English sentences with the supplied hinge "we must" (no Tibetan under it, left unwrapped). The two tshul are ruled separately: the first (de dgag pa'i tshul, 'the way of keeping them closed') heads the list and is absorbed into 'To keep ... closed we must, respectively'; the second (ltung ba 'byung tshul, 'the way a downfall arises') is what GMR renders 'when and how'. bslab pa (the trainings/precepts) is banked once as 'instructions', the object of gus pa 'respect for'; 'commitments' is the same word re-surfacing in GMR's gloss 'on how to keep these commitments' and is not double-banked. 'learn and', 'a deep', 'the laws of', 'the various', 'state of', 'that will work against', 'that happens to be our own' are translator's expansion and stay unwrapped.
C03/c3p171: AI NOTE — A bare Tibetan bibliographic note that GMR expands into two English sentences: the frame ('As for where to find instructions on', 'you can use a number of', 'Some examples would be his treatise called') is supplied and left unwrapped, as is every 'vows' (no sdom pa stands under any of them). The two book titles are banked whole as proper names, byang chub gzhung lam = Highway to Buddhahood and dngos grub snye ma = Golden Harvest of Attainments (GMR's title adds 'Golden'), with their members inside; English word order runs backwards against the Tibetan, hence eng_order. The opening byang sems is nulled rather than double-claiming the single 'bodhisattva', which belongs to the title clause.

AI NOTE — One Tibetan sentence rendered as three English sentences. The first book is named by its full title sdom gsum bslab bya nor bu'i 'od 'phreng, banked whole as a proper name; GMR renders it head-first (“advices on the three sets of vows known as the String of Shining Jewels”), so its members reverse inside it. The second reference (sngags byang sems kyi bslab bya'i sdoms tshig lta bu) is generic, “verse summaries of the secret and bodhisattva precepts and the like”, so it is walked flat. bslab bya occurs three times: “advices” in the title, unrendered in the genitive (GMR's “that teach about” is a hinge, not the word), and “presentations” as the anaphoric third, a loose but real exponent. ci lcogs las (“whatever you can manage”) is rendered as an availability-of-time clause. dgos is nulled: “at all costs” is GMR's intensifier, not the modal.

AI NOTE — GMR reorders heavily: de ltar ("as described") lands after the vows; clause-final yang is fronted as "even if" onto the whole concessive clause; mthar phyin pa precedes its object sa lam in English. dam sdom is left whole: HGM glosses dam tshig itself as "pledges and vows", so neither member can be honestly assigned one word of GMR's "vows and pledges". sa lam is split (HGM: "levels and paths"). ma thub is spanned whole against "unable" since "able" occurs twice. The first lam (of lam bskyed rdzogs) and byung have no separate exponent and are nulled.
C03/c3p172: AI NOTE — One gerundive chain ('thob cing … mjal … gyur te) that GMR renders as three sentences; cing and te have no exponent. brgyud mar and skye ba cross ("the string of your future lives"). "immense", "kind of", "actual", "put … into", "always" (both), "find yourself" and the gloss "one who teaches you the secret way" have no Tibetan under them and stay unwrapped. gsang sngags kyi lam is kept whole because "secret" occurs three times.

AI NOTE — Flat walk. skye ba bdun nam / skye ba bcu drug is a paired count; GMR renders skye ba once, so the second is nulled. tshun chad du ("up to") surfaces as "within", which GMR fronts to the first count. dma' mtha'ang is "even at the lowest" — GMR renders the same phrase "at least" in C03:578; here his "at the very most" states the consequence (a cap of sixteen) rather than the word, so it is left unwrapped rather than banked with inverted polarity. The supplied "As such you will ... be able to" and "has spoken the following" have no Tibetan under them. C16:505 carries the same passage with dma' mtha' (no 'ang).

AI NOTE — Four-line verse citation; the line-initial capitals (Then, Will, Within, The, Even, Does) are lineation. GMR's English reorders the last two lines against the Tibetan: ma bsgoms par yang ('even without meditating') precedes dngos grub thob in the Tibetan, while the English states the result first; eng_order carries the published order. dbang bskur occurs twice: the first is the noun 'empowerment', the second is split by GMR into 'the power ... given', so its two words are banked separately (dbang 'power', bskur 'given'). dang is a coordinator ('and'); the idiom skye dang skye bar comes out as 'life after life', but 'after' is not dang's meaning and stays unwrapped. Also unwrapped as GMR's supply: 'the person', 'is', 'A', 'Then', 'the', 'be', 'The', 'is', 'if the person Does'.
C03/c3p173: AI NOTE — Verse citation; line-initial capitals are lineation. GMR reorders across the four lines: 'keep' (dang ldan) precedes 'The meditation', and 'Will reach the goal' (dngos grub thob) is hoisted ahead of 'Within this life'. 'dir = 'di + locative -r, so 'Within this' is the whole word's exponent. The negated third line las dbang gis ma 'grub is recast as the concessive 'or, Past deeds preventing, At least' - only las 'deeds' has a pointable exponent; dbang gis, ma, 'grub are nulled. 'But', 'further', 'Their', 'Past', 'At least', 'Will' and the articles are GMR's supply and stay unwrapped.

AI NOTE — Verse citation; initial capitals mid-sentence are lineation. GMR's English reorders the two verse lines against the Tibetan (the goal line before the no-downfall condition), so eng_order carries the published order. The quotative ces dang opens the wylie but its English ("says as well") follows the speaker's name. "A person", "the length of", "should he", "has" and the articles are supplied hinges with no Tibetan under them. sgyur is left without English: the parallel witnesses (TCS13:730, TCS05:475) read ma bsgoms gyur, the auxiliary; see errata.

AI NOTE — Verse citation from the Book of the Five Pledges; the initial capitals on As and The goal are lineation of the quoted lines, not apparatus. GMR's The Book of ... concurs renders the citation frame (ces pa dang ... las kyang) idiomatically: Book and concurs have no one-to-one Tibetan exponent, so las and kyang are nulled rather than over-captured — kyang is 'as well', and the parallel at TCS05:475 renders the same frame with states that. The goal is is GMR's supplied subject and copula for the bare verb 'grub, so only reached is wrapped. Identical published reading at P1:128.
C03/c3p174: AI NOTE — GMR renders this sentence very freely. The opening citation frame (ces sogs gyud dang grub chen du mas lan cig ma yin par gsungs pas, 'because it has been taught more than once by the tantras and many mahasiddhas') has no exponent at all, and 'these facts' summarises the citation rather than rendering de 'dra'i bka', so both are nulled. rnyed par gur nas ('having come to find') is answered only loosely by 'come to know' / 'seek', and srog dang bsdos ('staking one's life') by the quoted 'even if it costs your life'; only srog = 'life' is banked. 'a kind of', 'in them', 'within you', 'could ever', 'your mind' and 'you must then protect your commitments' are GMR's supplied material and stay unwrapped.

AI NOTE — GMR turns one Tibetan conditional sentence into four English sentences. The opening question (What would it be to cost your life?) and the framing verbs Imagine / suppose he came up to you and said / I swear I will / Suppose it were are narrative scaffolding with no Tibetan under them and are left unwrapped. lta bu ('of the sort') carries only kind of; the some is GMR's supplied indefinite (it also precedes follower, which has none). khyod is banked as yours (vows of yours), the one unambiguous exponent of the possessor; the bare yous are the speaker's scaffolding. mi bsrun pa'i (lit. 'untamed') is cruel; really very is supplied. blos ma btang na is literally 'if you do not give it up' — the English recasts it as the positive alternative either you reject this morality, so btang carries reject and that clause's ma has no exponent. The two gsod are the threat (kill) and its outcome (die). dam thig is quoted as it stands in the source; it is a spelling of dam tshig (see errata).

AI NOTE — GMR's opening frame (At the "cost of your life" then your choice would go like this.) and closing line (I will never give up these morals.) have no Tibetan in this segment and stay unwrapped. ma bsod (not-kill) is rendered by the positive lexeme spare; 'gyur (become) is recast as reach and nulled rather than banked; rung (it is acceptable) carries let it be so, with kyang and ste around it unrendered.
C03/c3p175: AI NOTE — GMR folds the quoted resolve tshul khrims blos mi gtong snyam du into "if it comes down to" and splits the single Tibetan petition into three English sentences, so the English side crosses the Tibetan order freely (explicit eng_order). Structurally the object of bsrung "keep" is dam sdom, the contracted doublet, which GMR renders "vows and pledges"; the earlier full pair dam tshig dang sdom pa, object of gces spras, is summed up as the supplied resumptive "these commitments" and is therefore nulled rather than double-banked. gces spras takes the bare second "cherish", pinned by eng_order; the supplied pronoun and object stay unwrapped. tshe bar byas te is left without English: it reads as che bar byas te, "making them greater" (see errata), whose force GMR carries in "infinitely more than", claimed for lhag par du ... las. Supplied and unwrapped: "In short", "you had surely better", "The one thing", the whole "What you are requesting from your Lama is that he or she" hinge, "always", "your own precious", and the following section heading "XII. Meditating on the Two Secret Stages" glued onto the English (registered ingest class).

AI NOTE — Flat walk. GMR's framing (“This brings us to the … Step to training oneself in the secret half of the bodhisattva activities”, the preposition “upon”, “while one continues to”, “his”, and the whole second sentence about the root-text verse) has no Tibetan under it and is left unwrapped. gsum pa is a true ordinal here (“the third Step”), so “third” is claimed. gnas takes only “maintain”; the aspectual “continues to” is the translator's. The genitive 'i of bsgom pa'i is unclaimed.

AI NOTE — Verse (12) of the cited prayer, four Tibetan lines plus the colophon tail zhes pa'i oo ka gcig ste ("this is one shloka"), which the English does not render. Verse-line initial capitals are lineation, not apparatus. GMR re-lays the single Tibetan petition byin gyis rlobs as two petitions, "Bless me next" / "Grant me then"; it is banked once, as "Grant me", where it sits beside sgrub par "To practice" exactly as in the Tibetan. "Bless me", "then", "And", and the supplied tail "that there is" (for the comparative las) carry no Tibetan and stay unwrapped.
C03/c3p176: AI NOTE — Flat shape.
